# Psalm 146 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA (Council Arbiter) | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Praise the LORD! Praise the LORD, O my soul!

**2** I will praise the LORD as long as I live; I will sing praises to my God while I have my being.

**3** Put not your trust in princes, in a son of man, in whom there is no salvation.

**4** When his breath departs, he returns to the earth; on that very day his plans perish.

**5** Blessed is he whose help is the God of Jacob, whose hope is in the LORD his God,

**6** who made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them, who keeps faith forever;

**7** who executes justice for the oppressed, who gives food to the hungry. The LORD sets the prisoners free;

**8** the LORD opens the eyes of the blind. The LORD lifts up those who are bowed down; the LORD loves the righteous.

**9** The LORD watches over the sojourners; he upholds the fatherless and the widow, but the way of the wicked he brings to ruin.

**10** The LORD will reign forever, your God, O Zion, to all generations. Praise the LORD!

---
## Council Notes

SOPHIA detected **6** significant divergence(s) in Psalm 146.

- **146:2** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **146:9** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **146:10** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **146:4** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **146:5** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **146:8** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

## Translation Notes (Select)

### EMET
- **146:1**: First of the final Hallel psalms (146-150) — each begins and ends with 'Praise Yah' (Hallelujah).
- **146:7-9**: A catalogue of divine actions: justice, food, freedom, sight, lifting, love, protection — God's character expressed in concrete deeds for the vulnerable.

### LOGOS
- **146:3-4**: The anti-trust declaration: human leaders die and their plans die with them. Only God's reign endures. This frames the entire final Hallel.
- **146:7-9**: Jesus echoes these verses in Luke 4:18-19 and 7:22 — his ministry is the fulfillment of what this psalm attributes to God.

### PNEUMA
- **146:3-4**: Don't trust powerful people. Why? Because they die. And when they die, their plans die with them. Every four years this verse becomes profoundly relevant.
- **146:7-9**: This is God's résumé of action: justice, food, freedom, sight, support, love, protection. These aren't just theological ideas — they're things God actually does for real people in real need.

— SOPHIA
